summary: A 1971 note by P. M. Karp about a network meeting. It was updated by RFC 116.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo announces the next Network Working Group meeting and tells prospective attendees how to arrange hotel reservations. It is a logistical notice rather than a technical specification.

subtitle: A notice giving the place, time and room-reservation plan for a Network Working Group meeting.

tldr.problem: Members of the Network Working Group needed to know where and when their next meeting would take place.
tldr.mechanism: The notice gives the Atlantic City venue and meeting dates, and describes how MITRE would coordinate hotel reservations.
tldr.outcome: RFC 99 is a meeting notice and was updated by RFC 116.

facts.label: Meeting location
facts.value: Wicker Room, Dennis Hotel, Atlantic City

today: RFC 99 was updated by RFC 116. Its status is listed as Unknown in the unit metadata.

sections.title: Meeting Place and Schedule
sections.content: The next Network Working Group meeting is to be held in Atlantic City, New Jersey, coincident with the SJCC. The Wicker Room at the Dennis Hotel is reserved from Sunday, May 16 at 8:00 pm through Thursday, May 20 at 6:00 pm.
sections.plainLanguage: The notice tells members where the meeting will take place and when the reserved room will be available.

sections.title: Hotel Reservations
sections.content: Because a block of hotel rooms could not be reserved, the organizers plan to handle reservations through MITRE in an attempt to place attendees at the same hotel. Prospective attendees are asked to contact the author's secretary, Mrs. Marybelle Goodson.
sections.plainLanguage: Attendees should contact the named secretary to arrange a room. MITRE will try to place the group in the same hotel.

sections.title: Administrative Notice
sections.content: RFC 99 records meeting logistics rather than computer protocol rules. The unit metadata identifies RFC 116 as an update to this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC is a meeting announcement, not a set of technical rules. RFC 116 later updated it.
